dispute.riderClaim: The driver went far out of the way through the east side instead of heading straight to Marina Bay. The trip was much longer than the app's route, he stopped for a few minutes for no reason, and I was charged more. Please refund the extra charge.
dispute.driverStatement: I took the route I thought was faster at that time because the usual expressway is often jammed. The stop was short.

cases.summary: The driver took an alternative route to avoid congestion on the usual expressway, believing it faster at the time. GPS data shows a material detour under RD-1 (+2642 m, +33.2%, exceeding the 796 m threshold), and there was one 180-second stop. The driver's stated rationale (CTE jam) is a traffic-avoidance justification, but no documented road closure or navigation reroute supports it (RD-4 not met), and the rider objected twice rather than approving the route (RD-3 not met). The fare arithmetic is valid and the server-computed route-excess refund is S$1.98. The driver's position is that the detour was a reasonable operational judgment call, but under the demonstration policy the material detour triggers a route-excess refund.

The fare charged is arithmetically valid and matches the rate card; no billing anomaly exists.

cases.summary: The GPS trace shows the driver's actual route was 10,598 m against a reference route of 7,956 m, an excess of 2,642 m (+33.2%), far beyond the RD-1 materiality threshold of 796 m. The trip also took 418 s longer than the reference estimate and included one unexplained 180-second stop. The rider objected twice in chat during the trip and never approved the longer route, so RD-3 does not apply, and no documented closure or navigation reroute (RD-4) is in evidence. The rider is therefore entitled to a refund of the excess-distance charge, computed by the server as S$1.98 under RD-2.

arguments.claim: The detour was material under RD-1: actual distance 10,598 m vs reference 7,956 m, an excess of 2,642 m (+33.2%), exceeding the 796 m threshold.

Because the detour is material and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies, the eligible excess-distance charge must be refunded; the server computes S$1.98 (2,642 m x S$0.75/km x 1.0 surge, capped at the surged distance charge and amount paid).

The rider did not request or approve the longer route; the rider objected twice during the trip (CHAT-01 and CHAT-03) and the chat summary records no rider agreements and no rider route requests, so RD-3's keep_charge exception does not apply.
The trip was longer in both distance and time, and included one unexplained 180-second stop at 11:13:58Z, corroborating the rider's account that the trip took longer than the app's route.

counterevidence.claim: The driver stated the usual expressway (CTE) was jammed and claimed the alternate route was faster (CHAT-02). This is an uncorroborated assertion; no traffic or navigation data in evidence supports it, and the actual route was 418 s slower than the reference estimate, so it does not establish an RD-4 documented diversion.
The driver's history shows 3,400 completed trips and a 4.7 rating, but history is context only and cannot establish fault or override current-trip evidence.
The rider's history (4.9 rating, 210 trips, 1 dispute filed) is likewise context only and cannot establish fault.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. A detour is material when the actual route distance exceeds the reference route distance by more than the greater of 500 metres or 10% of the reference distance.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: Definition used by RD-2 and RD-5; no remedy on its own.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. When a detour is material under RD-1 and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies, refund the eligible excess-distance charge: excess metres x per-kilometre rate x surge multiplier, capped at the surged distance charge and at the amount paid. The server computes the amount.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: refund_route_excess when RD-1 is met and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due when the rider requested or expressly approved the longer route before or during the trip.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when the rider requested or approved the longer route.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due when a documented road closure, navigation reroute or equivalent diversion explains the longer route.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when a documented diversion explains the longer route.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due for a deviation that is not material under RD-1.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when RD-1 is not met.
